Rafael, we have an urgent issue. The client in Rotterdam sent a complaint this morning.
Oh no. What happened? Was the shipment late?
No, it arrived on time, but twenty boxes were damaged. The mangoes were too soft.
That is serious. I think we should find the root cause first.
I agree. The client thinks the cold container was too warm.
Then we should check the temperature records. Why don't we call the port in Santos?
Good idea. But we shouldn't wait too long. The client wants an answer today.
You're right. How about sending a short email now, and a full report on Friday?
Perfect. And we should have a backup plan for the next shipment.
Yes. If there is a shortage of containers, we can use a second company. We will fix this.
I think we should find the root cause first.
Why don't we call the client today?

When a client complains, many managers make the same mistakes. First, you shouldn't hide the problem. Clients always find out, and then the issue is bigger. Second, you shouldn't blame other people in the first call. Say sorry, and say that you are checking. Then you should find the root cause. Ask simple questions: what happened, when, and why? Next, you should give the client a date for a full answer, and keep it. Finally, and this is the step most companies forget, you should have a backup plan. If one supplier has a shortage, who can help you tomorrow? A problem is not always a disaster. A problem that is fixed quickly can make a client trust you more.

Hi Rafael, this is Paulo from the plant. I'm calling about an urgent issue. One of our main machines stopped this morning at six o'clock, and the production line is closed. Nobody was hurt, and the machine is not badly damaged. The technicians think the root cause is an old part. The good news is that we can fix it, but the new part arrives on Thursday. So we have a problem: our output will be lower this week, and we may have a shortage for two clients. I think we should call those clients today. Why don't we offer them iron from our stock in the other warehouse? Please call me back when you can. Thanks.

First, the client sends a complaint about the damaged boxes. Then, the team says sorry and checks the facts. Next, they find the root cause: the container was too warm. After that, they send the client a plan and a date for a full answer. Finally, they prepare a backup plan for the next shipment.
